public_sources.bound_semantics: RFC 9002 says resumed connections over the same network MAY use the previous connection's final smoothed RTT as the resumed connection's initial RTT; when no previous RTT is available a fresh initial RTT is used.

RFC 9000 normally resets RTT estimation on a new path, but allows retention when only the peer port changes, a common NAT-rebinding continuity case, while warning that retaining old state across materially different path characteristics can be too aggressive.

chat_native_reduction.mapping: Treat a validated same-scope/same-assignment continuity token as the limited continuity condition analogous only to a resumed same-network/port-only continuity case; all other epoch changes reset estimator state.
chat_native_reduction.extra_role_local_safety: Before enabling transferred state, require one fresh current-epoch same-scope probe with abs(probe-SRTT_old)<=1.0. This bounded drift check is an added controller guard, not a QUIC requirement.
chat_native_reduction.probe_rule: The continuity probe is qualification evidence; old estimator deadlines are not activated for the new epoch until the gate passes.

control_results.details: Same scope/assignment/token and fresh probe 2 satisfy drift bound. Warm-start old SRTT=2, RTTVAR=.5625 then probe update gives RTTVAR=.421875 and deadline=3.6875, preserving valid same-regime history.

credit_rule: At most one role-local credit after exact terminal readback; file creation alone earns zero credit.
scope_limit: Fixed synthetic epoch-rollover trace only. RFC 9000/9002 support conditional RTT-state reuse/reset semantics but do not define this controller's continuity token, drift threshold, durable persistence or prove production timeout correctness.
